messages:
support-jen: FYI customer Acme reported a big p99 jump after runtime v3.14 rolled 1h ago. They see 250ms -> ~900ms on long prompts. forwarding traces and request IDs.

alice: thanks. any canary signals? did canary pass?

deploy-bot: deploy v3.14 -> commit sha a1b2c3d deployed to canary and prod at 2026-03-17T09:12Z. Canary traffic 5%.

dmitri: I see a p99 delta in canaries in the last 30m — +600ms on a subset of requests that use KV-prefetch.

ben: sounds like KV cache path could be hitting a slow path. v3.14 included the new kernel-selector change (prefer-compute-kernel).

carol: pulling flamegraphs and tail traces now. can you paste a sample request id?

support-jen: request ids: req-ACME-78412, req-ACME-78456 (attached in thread). customer says pattern is >1k tokens + streaming.

carol: quick grep from the trace: kernel_selector.cpp: preferComputePath=true in stack for those requests. CPU wait spikes around kernel selection.

alice: aha — kernel selector change could add overhead per layer when kv cache hits are high. explains cost for long sequences.

ben: repro steps I ran locally: 
``` 
# reproduce with loadgen
python tools/loadgen.py --model gemini-small --seq 1200 --streaming true --batch-size 1 --warmup 50
```
I see p99 ~850ms with v3.14 vs ~230ms on v3.13.

dmitri: let's bisect the kernel selector change. suspect commit 9f4e2e that added `prefer_compute_kernel` flag.

alice: agree. quick mitigation: roll back that flag on canaries or flip to prefer_packed_kernel=true. Can we do a targeted rollout?

deploy-bot: can do a config rollback for canary pool. `reroute deploy v3.14 --override kernel_selector:prefer_compute_kernel=false --scope canary`

ben: before we flip, we should validate perf on the golden prompt set. I have a 12-item tail prompt set for Acme. Running tests now.

observability-bot: perf-check report: canary baseline (v3.13) p95=220ms p99=260ms; v3.14 canary p95=240ms p99=880ms (sample size 1200). Error rate stable.

carol: I captured a stack sample showing extra `compute_fallback()` calls per layer — looks like an extra sync introduced by the selector. attaching snippet: 
``` 
# stack sample
runtime::kernel_selector::select()
  runtime::kernel::compile()
  runtime::kv_cache::get()
  runtime::kernel::compute_fallback()
```

dmitri: ok plan: 1) roll kernel_selector flag back on canary; 2) run golden prompts to confirm; 3) schedule quick prod rollback if p99 improves; 4) bisect commit 9f4e2e to find minimal diff.

alice: I'm on the rollback, doing canary override now. ping me if you see drops.

deploy-bot: override applied to canary pool at 2026-03-17T09:28Z. kernel_selector:prefer_compute_kernel=false

carol: re-running golden set against canary...

observability-bot: post-override metrics (canary): p95=225ms p99=270ms (sample 600). trend looks back to baseline.

support-jen: relaying to customer: confirmed regression linked to runtime change; canary rollback restored baseline, planning prod rollback if no other failures. customer appreciated the quick response. :thumbsup:

ben: next steps: bisect 9f4e2e locally to identify the exact line that introduces the sync. also add a microbenchmark for kernel_selector to CI and add a perf-gate for p99 on our golden sets.

alice: I'll own the prod rollback decision after we validate canary for one more hour and get approval from eng-sre.

dmitri: logging action items: (a) bisect commit, (b) add regression test to perf CI, (c) add feature flag doc + rollout checklist, (d) follow up with Acme support ticket.

support-jen: updated ticket and put customer on status page watchlist. thanks team.

carol: saving traces and flamegraphs to the incident folder: s3://redwood-incidents/1839992000/kernel-selector-tail/

alice: nice work. once bisect identifies the culprit we can craft a minimal fix or optimize selector path. closing loop when prod decision is made. :white_check_mark:
